name: repairs nonfinite values without mutating inputs
test:
import numpy as np
image = np.array([[1., np.nan], [np.inf, 5.]])
result = analyze_image_dataset([image])
assert result['types'] == ['gray'] and result['noisy_indices'] == [0]
assert result['noisy_rate'] == 1.0
assert np.isfinite(result['cleaned'][0]).all()
assert np.isnan(image[0, 1]) and np.isinf(image[1, 0])

name: classifies channels and handles all-invalid or empty sets
test:
import numpy as np
all_bad = np.full((2, 2, 3), np.nan)
result = analyze_image_dataset([np.zeros((2, 2, 3)), all_bad, np.zeros((2, 2, 2))])
assert result['types'] == ['color', 'color', 'unknown']
assert np.equal(result['cleaned'][1], 0).all()
empty = analyze_image_dataset([])
assert empty['types'] == [] and empty['noisy_rate'] == 0.0

name: repair uses each array own mean and copies even clean arrays
test:
import numpy as np
dirty = np.array([[1., np.nan], [-np.inf, 5.]])
clean = np.array([[100., 200.]])
result = analyze_image_dataset([dirty, clean])
assert np.array_equal(result['cleaned'][0], [[1., 3.], [3., 5.]])
assert np.array_equal(result['cleaned'][1], clean)
assert not np.shares_memory(result['cleaned'][0], dirty)
assert not np.shares_memory(result['cleaned'][1], clean)
assert result['quality'] == {'total': 2, 'clean': 1}
assert result['noisy_indices'] == [0] and result['noisy_rate'] == 0.5
assert analyze_image_dataset([np.zeros(3), np.zeros((2, 2, 1))])['types'] == ['unknown', 'gray']
